text:
Alex: quick check — ran the 2k-seqlen throughput sweep on H100 vs A100 vs L40S and seeing a weird p95 regression on H100 for batch=8, fp16. table attached (summary):

Alex: H100: mean=12.8k toks/s, p95=13.0k, p99=14.1k
Alex: A100: mean=11.9k toks/s, p95=11.95k, p99=12.3k
Alex: L40S: mean=12.0k toks/s, p95=12.05k, p99=12.5k

Alex: the mean looks fine but H100 p95 is unexpectedly higher relative to mean (more variance). config: seq_len=2048, batch=8, kv-cache=on, flash-attn enabled, amp=fp16, CUDA 12.2, driver=535.86, model=redwood-xl-7b (quant disabled). Anyone seen this noise on H100 before? cc @Maria @Derek

Maria: I ran a subset earlier; saw some jitter on warmup windows. Two quick asks: 1) are these single-run numbers or aggregates? 2) can you share the exact run command + env?

Alex: single-run summary, sorry. command was: `./bench_runner --model redwood-xl-7b --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kv-cache --fp16 --flash-attn` on a fresh node. Logs uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/tmp/1758612345/h100-run.log

Derek: throwing profiler output here from a similar run on H100 yesterday — seems like occasional spikes in CUDA memcpy and kernel launch latency. snippet:```
GPU memcpy H2D: peaks ~4.2ms
Kernel launch jitter: 0.9ms -> 6.4ms (outliers)
SM util ~92% but stalls due to L2 congestion at those moments
Memory throughput ~430 GB/s (bursting)
```

Sasha: can we rule out NIC/oomkube scheduling? if the pod got migrated between NUMA domains you can see p95 tail spikes. also ask to run with `--no-kv-cache` and `--no-flash` to isolate. small runs (10 iters) with perf counters are helpful too.

Kevin: I can schedule an automated comparative job on perf-ci if we want reproducible runs across SKUs. name: `perf/schedule/sku-compare/1758612345`. Would you like 5 seeds per sku? Also confirm you want CUDA12.2 vs 12.1 parity?

Alex: yes please Kevin — 5 seeds per sku. keep CUDA/driver the same if possible. set MIG off for A100 (whole GPU). include both kv-cache on/off.

Maria: noted — I'll also re-run locally on A100 with cuda 12.1 to check driver-induced behavior. one more thing: what quant/conv kernels are loaded? `torch.version` and `triton`?

Alex: torch=2.2.1+cu12, triton=2.0.0, flash-attn v2, kernel-lib built with `-O3 -arch=compute_90` on H100.

infra-bot: perf job queued: perf-ci://jobs/1758612345-sku-compare (5 runs per sku). expected ETA ~ 2h. I'll post results here when done. :gear:

Derek: when infra results land, please include full p50/p95/p99 + sample stddev and the raw lat distribution histogram. P95 without distribution is misleading for regen checks.

Sasha: quick debugging tip: run `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/local/lib/libjemalloc.so` again — we saw allocator-induced pauses before. also check `nvidia-smi dmon` during run.

Kevin: scheduled with CUDA 12.2 image and an alternative 12.1 image (two matrix runs) so we can bisect driver impact. I'll pin the commit hash used by bench_runner in the job metadata.

Alex: awesome — thanks all. I'll wait for infra-bot to post the CI artifacts and then we'll decide next steps (kv-cache vs kernel tuning). If the H100 p95 remains, I can collect nsight traces for a couple of outlier iterations.

Maria: if you capture nsight, ping me — I can help analyze kernel timelines.

infra-bot: perf job started: perf-ci://jobs/1758612345-sku-compare/run-1

Alex: closing loop for now — will follow up with artifacts. :eyes:
